Subject: Re: Intro / MAP kickoff - MedInsights evaluation

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. I promised to sketch a short mutual action plan so our internal stakeholders (product, security, procurement) can see what success looks like for this evaluation. Attached is a one-page MAP and a rough calendar. A few things we want to validate during the trial:

- Accuracy of triage classification on our 20k sample (precision target >= 92%)
- Average p99 latency under 300ms for 512-token requests
- Evidence of KV/prefix caching reducing token cost by at least 22% over baseline

Can you confirm how Redwood plans to measure those — and what acceptance tests you recommend? Our procurement team also needs a security questionnaire answered before we turn on a dedicated environment (cc'ing them).

Next steps we propose:
1) Scoped test dataset delivered by end of next week (Jun 21)
2) Two-week sandbox evaluation (Jun 24 - Jul 8)
3) Decision review and go/no-go on Jul 9

Appreciate any test templates or exit gate wording you can share.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Product Operations
MedInsights

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Intro / MAP kickoff - MedInsights evaluation

Alex — thanks for the clear outline and the attachments. Linking a concise acceptance plan below so legal/procurement and product can align quickly. I attached a slightly expanded MAP matrix (column definitions and owners).

Quick answers to your three validation points and the acceptance tests we suggest:

1) Accuracy (precision >= 92%)
- Acceptance test: run labeled holdout (2k records) during sandbox week; threshold = precision >= 92% across critical labels; test run by MedInsights with Redwood verifying logs and sampling.
- Exit gate: pass on 3 consecutive sample batches or escalate to product review if 2/3 fail.

2) Latency (p99 < 300ms for 512 tokens)
- Acceptance test: synthetic and replay traffic (1k qps bursts) measured by Redwood runtime with distributed tracing.
- Exit gate: p99 below 300ms sustained for 30m under representative load OR documented mitigation plan + staged rollback window.

3) Cost savings (token delta via caching)
- Acceptance test: run two traffic slices (with/without prefix cache) for 48 hours; compare per-token billing and cache hit rates.
- Exit gate: >22% reduction in per-token cost OR approval for quantized model trial as interim.

Owners and responsibilities
- MedInsights: provide labeled sample set + procurement clearance (Procurement contact)
- Redwood (Ben): implement caching configs and provide test harness + perf scripts
- Redwood (Grace): run operational smoke tests, evidence capture, and dashboarding for decision review

Proposed timeline (fine-grained)
- Jun 18: MedInsights shares labeled sample (2k holdout) and dataset schema
- Jun 21: Redwood delivers MAP_v1 with test harness and dashboard links
- Jun 24 - Jul 6: Sandbox evaluation (perf + accuracy + cost runs)
- Jul 7: Buffer day for remediation (if any)
- Jul 9: Review + go/no-go

If this looks good I can convert the MAP_v1 to a shared spreadsheet and create the HubSpot kickoff. Also: procurement — please review the attached security questionnaire and flag any blockers.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-15 08:27 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / MAP kickoff - MedInsights evaluation

Alex / Mina — quick technical notes on the acceptance tests so engineering can prep the harness:

- For the accuracy run: we'll provide a small pytest-style evaluation script that ingests MedInsights labels and emits a single report (precision/recall/F1 by label). We'll also produce seed samples and the sampling plan.
- For latency: we need representative request distribution (seq_len histogram). If you can share a week of anonymized traces (or a histogram) that will help us size the burst tests.
- For caching: we'll expose cache hit/miss metrics in the dashboard (and raw KV metrics in logs) so cost calculation is auditable.

Operational checklist (to avoid surprises):
1) API keys scoped to sandbox (no production cross-traffic)
2) Toggle for prefix cache disabled/enabled per slice
3) Instrumented tracing (OpenTelemetry) hooked to your SRE team

I'll drop the test harness repo link in the shared HubSpot note once Mina creates it. Ben

--
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rayo <alex.rayo@medinsights.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@medinsights.com>

Subject: Re: Intro / MAP kickoff - MedInsights evaluation

Alex / team — thanks, all. Final confirmation and next steps:

- Mina: I'll convert the attached MAP_v1 into the shared spreadsheet by EOD and invite the stakeholders.
- Ben: test harness repo and perf scripts will be posted to the HubSpot record by Jun 18 12:00 PT.
- Grace: I'll run the first smoke test on Jun 24 morning and send the dashboard link immediately after.
- MedInsights procurement: once you confirm the security questionnaire is complete, we can provision the sandbox keys (scoped) and the dataset upload instructions.

Decision criteria recap (short):
- Accuracy: holdout precision >= 92% on critical labels
- Latency: p99 < 300ms for 512 tokens under representative bursts
- Cost: per-token cost reduction via cache >= 22%

If all three gates pass on the review date (Jul 9) we will move to a 30-day pilot with reserved capacity and SLA targets. If any gate fails, we'll categorize the blocker (safety/regression/perf/cost) and propose either a remediation sprint (7-14 days) or a temporary fallback (smaller model / reduced batch size) depending on severity.

Thanks — looking forward to starting.
Mina
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
